s1.syndrome_frame: Acute hip pain and difficulty walking in an elderly patient with a history of osteoporosis and previous hip surgery
salient_findings: Incomplete transverse fracture in the lateral cortex of the right femoral neck
key_facts: 76-year-old woman
One week of right hip pain
Difficulty walking
Received denosumab for osteoporosis for five years
Underwent total hip arthroplasty for a left femoral neck fracture two years earlier
JOA score was 96 on the right and 76 on the left
Initial plain radiographs were reportedly normal
Repeat radiographs demonstrated an incomplete transverse fracture in the lateral cortex of the right femoral neck
Bone mineral density was 0.840 g/cm2 in the lumbar spine and 0.899 g/cm2 in the right femoral neck
Laboratory studies revealed calcium 9.7 mg/dL, phosphorus 3.9 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase 47 IU/L

shortlist.label: Atypical femoral fracture
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of denosumab use and presented with an incomplete transverse fracture in the lateral cortex of the right femoral neck

shortlist.label: Osteoporotic fracture
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of osteoporosis and low bone mineral density

shortlist.label: Stress fracture
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with hip pain and difficulty walking after a period of normal activity

shortlist.label: Denosumab-related fracture
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of denosumab use, which is a known risk factor for atypical femoral fractures

shortlist.label: Insufficiency fracture
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of osteoporosis and presented with a fracture in a weakened bone

shortlist.label: Femoral neck fracture
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with a fracture in the lateral cortex of the right femoral neck

shortlist.label: Osteonecrosis of the femoral head
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of hip surgery and presented with hip pain

shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of osteoporosis and presented with a fracture in a weakened bone

raw.rationale: The patient's history of long-term denosumab use, the presence of an incomplete transverse fracture in the lateral cortex of the right femoral neck, and the absence of comminution are consistent with an atypical femoral fracture.

rejected.label: Osteoporotic fracture
rejected.why: While the patient has osteoporosis, the specific characteristics of the fracture, such as its transverse orientation and lack of comminution, are more suggestive of an atypical femoral fracture.

rejected.label: Stress fracture
rejected.why: Stress fractures typically occur in younger, more active individuals and are often associated with a history of repetitive stress or overuse, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Denosumab-related fracture
rejected.why: While denosumab use is a risk factor for atypical femoral fractures, 'denosumab-related fracture' is not a specific diagnosis and is encompassed by the more precise diagnosis of atypical femoral fracture.

rejected.label: Insufficiency fracture
rejected.why: Insufficiency fractures occur when a normal stress is applied to a bone that is weakened by an underlying condition, but the patient's bone mineral density, although low, does not solely account for the specific type of fracture described.

rejected.label: Femoral neck fracture
rejected.why: The fracture is specifically described as being in the lateral cortex of the femoral neck, which is more characteristic of an atypical femoral fracture than a typical femoral neck fracture.

rejected.label: Osteonecrosis of the femoral head
rejected.why: There is no mention of osteonecrosis or avascular necrosis in the vignette, and the imaging findings do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pathologic fracture
rejected.why: Pathologic fractures occur in bones that are weakened by an underlying disease process, such as a tumor, which is not indicated in the vignette.
